CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), includes:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and
e. evaluation.
3. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), is in order to realize the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence in accordance with minimum service standards implemented by SKPD/UKPD and the community.

Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

Article 13

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

CHAPTER I

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing women victims of acts of violence.

REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.

13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

CHAPTER IV

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Article 6

The obligations and responsibilities in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence are the shared responsibility of:
a. Regional Government;
b. Community;
c. Family; and
d. Parents.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

Article 8

a. preventing the occurrence of acts of violence against women and children;
b. providing information and/or reporting acts of violence against women and children to law enforcement or authorized parties; and
c. participating in the handling of victims of acts of violence.
3. Forms of community participation as referred to in paragraph (2), shall be carried out responsibly in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, the following terms shall mean:

1. Region is the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DKI Jakarta Province.
2. Regional Government is the Governor and Regional Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province as elements of the administration of DKI Jakarta Province government.
3. Regional House of Representatives of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta, hereinafter referred to as DPRD, is a regional representative institution of the people as an element of regional government administration.
4. Governor is the Regional Head of DKI Jakarta Province who by virtue of his/her position also serves as the representative of the Government in the territory of DKI Jakarta Province.
5. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as SKPD, is the Apparatus of DKI Jakarta Province.
6. Regional Apparatus Work Unit, hereinafter abbreviated as UKPD, is the Regional Apparatus Work Unit of DKI Jakarta Province.
7. Discrimination is any distinction, harassment or exclusion, whether direct or indirect, based on human differences on the grounds of religion, ethnicity, race, ethnic group, social status, economic status, gender, language, political beliefs that result in the reduction, deviation or elimination of recognition, implementation or use of human rights and fundamental freedoms in life, whether individual or collective, in the political, economic, legal, social, cultural and other aspects of life.
8. Violence is any act unlawfully with or without the use of means against physical and psychological that causes danger to life, body or results in the deprivation of a person's freedom.
9. Violence against women is any act based on gender differences that results in or may result in suffering or harm to women physically, sexually or psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including threats of certain acts, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of freedom, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
10. Violence against children is any act against a child that results in suffering or harm physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically, economic or social exploitation, including neglect and ill-treatment that threatens bodily integrity and degrades the dignity of the child.
11. Domestic violence is any act against a person, especially women, that results in suffering or harm physically, sexually, psychologically and/or domestic neglect including threats to commit acts of coercion or deprivation of freedom unlawfully within the scope of the household.
12. Trafficking in Persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, transfer, harboring, receipt of a person by means of threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud and abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payments or benefits, so as to obtain the consent of a person having control over another person, whether conducted within the country or between countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in a person being exploited.
13. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years including a child still in the womb.
14. Woman is a person (human being) who has a vagina, can menstruate, become pregnant, give birth to children, and breastfeed.
15. Victim of violence is an individual or group of people who suffer physically, mentally or emotionally, economic loss, or experience neglect, reduction or deprivation of their basic rights, as a result of human rights (HAM) violations, or criminal acts as well as acts of violence committed either by state apparatus or by the state or regional government apparatus or by individuals, including the victim's heirs.
16. Protection is a series of fulfillment of the rights of women and child victims of violence and discrimination starting from prevention, handling and empowerment efforts.
17. Prevention is a direct effort undertaken by the Regional Government to prevent acts of violence against women and children.
18. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an Integrated Service Unit established by the Regional Government to provide services to women and child victims of violence comprehensively including information services, legal assistance and accompaniment, counseling services, medical services and safe houses through referral.
19. Task Force for the Prevention and Handling of Trafficking in Persons Crimes, hereinafter referred to as the Task Force, is a coordinating institution tasked with coordinating prevention and handling efforts of trafficking in persons crimes in DKI Jakarta Province.
20. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
21. Family are persons who have blood relations in direct ascending or descending line and collateral line up to the third degree, or who have marital relations, or persons who are dependents of women and/or children.
22. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations and/or community organizations.

To Enact:
REGIONAL REGULATION CONCERNING THE PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN FROM ACTS OF VIOLENCE.

I. GENERAL

The position of DKI Jakarta Province as the national capital as stipulated in Law Number 29 of 2007 concerning the Government of the Special Capital Region Province of Jakarta as the Capital of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia, makes the city of Jakarta an attraction for some members of the community from various regions, thus giving rise to various social problems, including acts of violence against women and children both within the household and outside the household, such as torture or treatment that can degrade human dignity and worth.

Various acts of violence both against women and children both within the household and outside the household will destroy family life, society, government, nation, and state, therefore the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta is obliged to provide protection to women and children from acts of violence which is an implementation of several laws and regulations, including Law Number 39 of 1999 concerning Human Rights, Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, Law Number 21 of 2007 concerning the Eradication of the Criminal Act of Trafficking in Persons, Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection.

Protection of women and children from acts of violence is one of the obligations of the Regional Government as regulated in Article 22 letter a of Law Number 32 of 2004 concerning Regional Government. On that basis, the Provincial Government of DKI Jakarta has made various efforts to protect women and children from acts of violence, but has not been able to provide protection to women and children from various acts of violence, among others due to the still low understanding of the community regarding the rights of women and children, handling has not been well coordinated, its implementation has not been sustainable, and so on. Therefore, a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence is needed to provide legal certainty in the protection of women and children from acts of violence.

The Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Women and Children from Acts of Violence, gives responsibility to the Regional Government from the prevention of acts of violence to the handling of victims of acts of violence. In its implementation the Regional Government cooperates with government agencies, other regional governments, and the community. In addition, adequate funding support both from the Government, Regional Government, as well as the participation of the business sector and the community, it is expected that violence against women and children can be eliminated.

Article 16

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children from acts of violence, the Regional Government shall establish P2TP2A as an integrated service center in the protection of women and children from acts of violence including victims of acts of violence.
2. P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), functions as an integrated service center in providing protection to women and children from acts of violence.
3. Further provisions regarding the Organization and Work Procedures of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (1), shall be stipulated by Governor Regulation.

Article 21

2. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) is conducted through:
a. notification of employment opportunity information for women victims of acts of violence;
b. education and training for women victims of acts of violence;
c. educational assistance for women and children victims of acts of violence who have been withdrawn from their education; and
d. fostering and enhancing women victims of acts of violence.
3. Partnership as referred to in paragraph (1) and paragraph (2), shall be set forth in the form of an agreement.

Article 20

1. In order to achieve the objectives of protection of women and children from acts of violence as referred to in Article 3, the Regional Government cooperates with:
